'''Herbert Keyshawn Jones''' (born October 6, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a senior in 2021, when he was also named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]].

Jones was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2022 and [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] in 2024.

==High school career==
Jones started playing [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball as a seventh-grader for Sunshine High School in [[Newbern, Alabama]], where his father served as the head coach. He played alongside his older brother, Walter Jr., and helped his team reach the Class 1A state finals in 2015, before the school closed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Champlin |first1=Drew |title=Small town standout Herb Jones has big basketball dreams |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/10/hale_county_standout_herb_jone.html |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 4, 2016}}</ref> For his junior season, Jones transferred to [[Hale County High School]] in nearby [[Moundville, Alabama]], following his father, who was an assistant coach.<ref name="tsoukalas">{{cite web |last1=Tsoukalas |first1=Tony |title=How a brotherly bond has always fueled Alabama freshman Herbert Jones |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/how-a-brotherly-bond-has-always-fueled-alabama-freshman-herbert-jones |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 16, 2021 |date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 16.6 points, 8.2 rebounds and four assists, earning Class 4A Player of the Year honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chandler |first1=Joey |title=Jones, Ford win Class 4A Player of the Year honors |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/sports/20170404/jones-ford-win-class-4a-player-of-year-honors |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=April 4, 2017}}</ref> Jones led Hale County to the 4A state championship, its first-ever state title.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Estwick |first1=Gary |title=Kaddell Perry, Herb Jones lead Hale County past Monroe County for 1st state title |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/kaddell-perry-alabama-commit-herb-jones-lead-hale-county-boys-to-first-ever-class-4a-crown/ |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=March 3, 2017}}</ref> He committed to playing college basketball at [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Champlin |first1=Drew |title=Hale County guard Herb Jones commits to Alabama |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/10/herb_jones_hale_county_alabama.html |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 6, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Alabama, Jones averaged 4.2 points and 3.5 rebounds per game. He drew a single-season program record 23 charges.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=Herbert Jones 'means a tremendous amount' to Tide basketball |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Herbert-Jones-means-a-tremendous-amount-to-Crimson-Tide-program-124468527/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=November 9, 2018}}</ref> In his sophomore season, he averaged 6.4 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.<ref name=martin>{{cite magazine |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Herb Jones' Offensive Development Could Be X-Factor for Crimson Tide Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/herb-jones-offensive-development-could-be-x-factor-for-crimson-tide |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 26, 2020}}</ref> On January 29, 2020, during a game against [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], Jones suffered a fractured left wrist and underwent surgery three days later. He returned to action on February 12 while wearing a cast on his wrist.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Byington |first1=Alex |title=How Alabama's one-handed Herb Jones showed 'warrior' approach returning to the floor against Auburn |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2020/02/13/how-alabama-basketballs-one-handed-herb-jones-showed-warrior-approach-return-vs-auburn/4751983002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> In his next game, after three days, Jones recorded six points and 17 rebounds in an 88–82 win over LSU. Late in the game, he made two free throws using only his right hand, due to his injury.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Walsh |first1=Christopher |title=Alabama Still Getting 'Goosebumps' From Epic Herb Jones Free Throws |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-goosebumps-herb-jones-free-throws |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 18, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, Jones averaged 7.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game and was a [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Defensive Team selection. He declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] before withdrawing and returning to college.<ref name=martin/><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Alabama Basketball's Herbert Jones Returning For Senior Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-basketballs-herbert-jones-returning-for-senior-season |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=June 3, 2020}}</ref>

At the close of the 2020–21 regular season, Jones was named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year by the league's coaches.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/31030484/2021-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|title=2021 SEC Men's Basketball Awards Announced|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 11.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. On April 8, 2021, Jones declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his extra year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Alabama Basketball's Herb Jones Officially Declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabamas-herb-jones-officially-declares-for-2021-nba-draft |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=April 8, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Jones was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 35th pick by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=2021 NBA Draft: New Orleans Pelicans select Alabama's Herbert Jones |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/2021-NBA-Draft-New-Orleans-Pelicans-select-Alabama-Crimson-Tide-Basketball-Herbert-Jones-168476679/ |access-date=August 1, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> On December 28, 2021, Jones scored a then career-high 26 points in a 108–104 win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers vs. Pelicans - Game Summary - December 28, 2021 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401360332 |access-date=2022-04-05 |publisher=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On March 27, 2022, he had a career-high six steals in a 116–108 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs New Orleans Pelicans Mar 27, 2022 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-nop-0022101119 |access-date=2022-04-05 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> Jones was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie second team]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eichenhofer |first1=Jim |title=Herbert Jones earns spot on NBA’s All-Rookie second team |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/herbert-jones-earns-spot-on-nbas-all-rookie-second-team |website=NBA |access-date=April 30, 2024 |date=May 18, 2022}}</ref>
On April 5, 2023, Jones put up a career-high 35 points to go with five made three-pointers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pelicans-news-knicks-record-never-seen-in-nba-history-matched-on-same-day|title=Knicks record never seen in NBA history matched by Pelicans on same day|website=ClutchPoints|last=Meyers|first=Andrew|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 5, 2023}}</ref> Following the season, Jones became a [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]] and re-signed with New Orleans to a four-year, $54 million contract.
On May 21, 2024, Jones was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team, as the only non-center to be included.<ref>https://www.nba.com/news/history-all-defensive-team</ref>
Jones made 20 starts for New Orleans during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 10.3 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 3.3 assists. On January 10, 2025, Jones was ruled out indefinitely after suffering a torn [[glenoid labrum|posterior labrum]] in his right shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelicans' Herb Jones out indefinitely with torn laburm|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/pelicans-herb-jones-out-indefinitely-with-torn-labrum-in-his-shoulder-211837845.html|access-date=January 12, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> On February 12, Jones was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing successful shoulder surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Herb Jones undergoes successful surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/herb-jones-medical-update-surgery-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-update-2-12-2025|access-date=February 13, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>
On July 14, 2025, Jones agreed to a three-year, $68 million contract extension with New Orleans.<ref>{{cite web | last=Nagel | first=Cody | title=Pelicans, forward Herbert Jones agree to three-year, $68 million extension, per report | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-07-11 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pelicans-forward-herbert-jones-agree-to-three-year-68-million-extension-per-report/ | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones is the son of Walter Sr. and Verlander Jones. He was born with [[hemolytic anemia]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burger |first1=Kyle |title=Alabama basketball player Herbert Jones fighting blood disorder since birth |url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/alabama-s-herbert-jones-fighting-since-birth/26542223 |publisher=[[WVTM-TV]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 26, 2019}}</ref> His older brother, Walter Jr., played college basketball for [[Texas–Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|Texas–Rio Grande Valley]] and [[Alabama A&M Bulldogs basketball|Alabama A&M]].<ref name=tsoukalas/>

Upon being drafted by the Pelicans, Jones is known for driving the same car every game as he did in his college days. Back then, he was also trying to save his money to help his family financially, by avoiding spending his own money, wearing the team's gear to every game.
